hook: I found the $26 upgrade to that viral $16 light

scenes.visual_prompt: Plug-in sconce glowing fixed warm-amber, static, no change
scenes.voiceover: The viral $16 sconce gives you one warm tone, fixed. That's all you get.

scenes.visual_prompt: Govee RGBIC LED strip behind a console table, colors shifting segment by segment
scenes.voiceover: For $26.09, this LED strip lets individual sections shift color and brightness independently — not the whole strip in one tone.

scenes.visual_prompt: Phone screen showing the Govee app scheduling the lights to switch on at dusk
scenes.on_screen_text: Set it to turn on at dusk. From your phone.
scenes.voiceover: You schedule it from your phone to switch on at dusk, same as the sensor built into the cheap sconces.

scenes.visual_prompt: Strip applied along the back of a wall mirror, indirect glow visible, no visible light source
scenes.on_screen_text: Indirect glow, not a visible bulb
scenes.voiceover: Mounted behind a mirror or along a doorframe, it creates that indirect glow-behind-an-object look instead of a visible fixture.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card comparing price and features: $16 fixed color vs $26.09 tunable, app-controlled
scenes.on_screen_text: Double the price. Not double for no reason.
scenes.voiceover: It's roughly double the price of the sconce, but it's for people who already know they want to control the color themselves.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final shot: full styled corner with the strip glowing warm-amber to match the sconce look
scenes.on_screen_text: Same vintage-glow look. Way more control.
scenes.voiceover: You can still land on that exact vintage-sconce color — you just get to choose it instead of accepting whatever the sconce ships with.

caption: The $16 plug-in sconce only comes in one fixed warm tone. This $26.09 strip gets you the same glow with full color and schedule control from your phone. Worth the upgrade? I break down the spec differences on the blog — link in bio.
